plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial producing large, fragrant, bowl-shaped to double flowers on sturdy stems above glossy, deeply divided foliage. A beloved cottage garden and cut-flower favorite that can live for decades.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (May to early June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Siberia, Mongolia, and northern China; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Peonies are often visited by ants that feed on sugary nectar on the buds, but contrary to myth, the ants are not required for the flowers to open.

plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A deciduous shrub bearing dense, cone-shaped clusters of intensely fragrant tiny flowers. In cooler northern regions, late-blooming varieties are at peak or finishing around this date.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (late April to late May in cooler northern regions)
plants.location: Native to the Balkan Peninsula; cultivated throughout cool temperate regions of Europe, North America, and northern Asia
plants.funFact: Lilac belongs to the olive family (Oleaceae), making it a relative of jasmine and ash trees.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: A compact, suckering shrub rose with fragrant, semi-double to double flowers and golden stamens. One of the oldest cultivated roses, it blooms in a single glorious flush in late spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to central and southern Europe and western Asia; grown in heritage gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Rosa gallica was used by ancient Romans and later medieval apothecaries, and dried petals retain their fragrance for years, making them prized for potpourri.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, graceful tree with fern-like foliage that bursts into billowing clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, carpeting the ground beneath. In the Northern Hemisphere subtropics it blooms in late spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June) in the Northern Hemisphere; October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); planted in Los Angeles, Mexico City, Pretoria, Lisbon, Sydney, and other warm regions
plants.funFact: In Mexico City, jacaranda blossoms in spring turn the streets purple, and in Pretoria, South Africa, the tree is so abundant that the city is nicknamed the Jacaranda City.

plants.name: Digitalis purpurea
plants.description: A biennial with tall spires of tubular, bell-shaped flowers spotted inside, adored by bumblebees. It thrives in woodland clearings, hedgerows, and cottage gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (May to July)
plants.location: Native to western and southwestern Europe and northwest Africa; naturalized in parts of North America, New Zealand, and Australia
plants.funFact: All parts of foxglove are highly toxic, yet it is the original source of digoxin, a heart medication still used today.
